messages:
maya: quick sync — we keep seeing high tail latency on dashboard queries when a tenant has a lot of short-lived access tokens. thinking we should split the authz filtering into a lightweight fast-path and a heavyweight aggregate path. thoughts?

sam: +1 on splitting. current authz check replays per-row which is killing p99 when page size increases.

jordan: curious what you mean by fast-path — an ACL index that can be checked pre-fanout? or a bloom-filter style prefilter? :thinking_face:

maya: prefilter + short-circuit. idea: maintain a per-tenant permissive-prefix index (small in-memory) that answers "all visible?"/"none visible?". only fall back to full policy evaluation for mixed cases.

leo: that sounds promising. tradeoff is memory and staleness window. how long until ACL changes must be respected?

maya: target is 1s-ish for eventual consistency for admin changes. we'd invalidate entries on writes. worst-case we fall back to full evaluation if uncertain.

sam: we should also consider RBAC scope expansion — many queries add filters that widen candidate set and the index loses usefulness. maybe we keep the index at the tenant->resource-level rather than query-level.

jordan: also need to think about cached aggregation results. if we cache aggregated panels, invalidation surface becomes large (ACL changes, data writes, config toggles). maybe keep caches scoped to read-only dashboards first.

maya: agreed. proposal: 1) fast-path index at tenant-resource granularity, LRU with admission based on access frequency; 2) keep aggregated panel cache but only for panels marked "stable" (opt-in by product); 3) fallback to existing per-row authz for mixed cases.

leo: what about query routing? if we have dedicated read nodes for cached aggregates vs heavy authz evaluation nodes, we can route. that helps SLOs.

sam: routing is good but needs capacity planning. can we simulate via canary where a subset of requests are steered to new path and compare p95/p99 costs?

maya: yes — infra-bot: created feature-flag "authz-fastpath" for canary testing.

infra-bot: Feature flag "authz-fastpath" created. rollout: canary 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%. Monitoring: p95 latency, p99 latency, query CPU, authz eval rate.

jordan: perf targets? current p99 for heavy dashboards ~ 1.8s. target with fast-path is <= 900ms for canary population. conservative target for GA is p99 <= 1s.

leo: cost tradeoff: index memory + eviction churn vs saved CPU on authz eval. we should model for top 100 tenants by qps. I can run a sim with heap sizes.

sam: also watch for throttling anomalies — fast-path could amplify hot-tenant issues (more requests returned faster -> downstream panels request more). maybe add a per-tenant concurrency cap and backpressure.

maya: good call. add concurrency cap + circuit breaker that falls back to full-eval when fast-path rejects due to cap.

jordan: small implementation note — keep the fast-path lookup monotonic and cheap: single hash lookup + generation check. sample code sketch:```go
// tenantIndex.Lookup(resource) -> (visibility, gen)
if vis == ALL { return early }
if vis == MIXED { fallback }
if gen < tenantEpoch { fallback }
```

sam: love the sketch. ensure we emit metrics: fastpath_hits, fastpath_misses, fastpath_evictions, fallback_count.

maya: rollout plan: spike canary for 24h on non-prod with recorded traces, then 1% prod for 6h, then 10% for 24h with alarms on p99>1.2s or error rate > 0.5%. if stable, expand.

leo: action items: I'll run memory/cost sim against top 100 tenants (due Thu). sam will wire metrics and add per-tenant cap (due Wed). jordan will prototype index API and push PR to eng-platform feature branch (due Tue). maya will draft the RFC follow-up documenting invariants and invalidation semantics.

maya: any objections? if not I'll post RFC follow-up and create the canary dashboard. :shipit:

sam: no objections from me.

jordan: fine by me.

leo: go for it."
